chunks: If his insanity reaches the point where he does not recognize the times of salat (prayer), they are to be separated. But if he recognizes the times of salat (prayer), then the woman should remain patient with him, for she has been tested.

key_terms.أَوْقَاتَ: the appointed times or prescribed periods
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), used here as a measure of awareness and discernment
key_terms.الْجُنُونُ: insanity or mental derangement affecting legal and marital judgment
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman or wife in the marriage
key_terms.بُلِيَتْ: she has been tested or afflicted with a trial
key_terms.فَلْتَصْبِرِ: let her be patient; an instruction to endure with sabr
key_terms.فُرِّقَ: they are separated; a ruling of marital separation

ai.seo_question: When does insanity justify separation between spouses in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion in a marital case involving insanity: if the condition becomes so severe that the man no longer recognizes the times of salat (prayer), separation is warranted. If he still recognizes the times of salat (prayer), the wife is instructed to show patience, framing her situation as a divine test.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "If his insanity reaches the point where he no longer recognizes the times of prayer, they are to be separated. However, if he still recognizes the times of prayer, the woman should remain patient with him, for she has been tested."
